title: Responsive Web Design Small Examples
description: Use these small Responsive Web Design examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Let the page use the device width
examples.description: A viewport is the area a browser uses to show a page.
examples.code:
A page for any screen

Start with the space you have.
examples.output: A mobile browser uses the device width instead of a wide pretend desktop page.

examples.title: Use a flexible content width
examples.description: A box can use most of the available width while also having a maximum width.
examples.code:
Reading club

This content stays away from the screen edges.
examples.output: The main area has side space on narrow screens and stops growing after 60rem.

examples.title: Let pictures shrink
examples.description: A responsive image can shrink to fit its parent while keeping its shape.
examples.code: In your project, apply this rule to a real image with width and height attributes.
examples.output: Images using this rule stay within their parent width. Their shape is kept instead of being stretched.

examples.title: Wrap a row of items
examples.description: Flexbox can wrap items onto a new row when there is not enough space.
examples.code:
Stories
Poems
Science
examples.output: The boxes share a row when space allows and wrap when it becomes narrow.

examples.title: Make a grid that fits
examples.description: An auto-fit grid chooses how many columns can fit.
examples.code:
Book A
Book B
Book C
examples.output: The number of columns changes with the space. Each card can shrink to the full available width on a very narrow screen.

examples.title: Add one larger-screen rule
examples.description: A media query applies styles only when a viewport rule matches.
examples.code:
Story

Main reading.

Related books
examples.output: The content stacks below 48rem. Wider screens show a main column and a smaller side column.

examples.title: Let text grow within limits
examples.description: clamp chooses a value between a minimum and maximum.
examples.output: The heading scales with the viewport but stays between 1.5rem and 3rem.

examples.title: Give controls room
examples.description: Touch users need controls that are easy to select.
examples.output: The two buttons have roomy targets and a clear gap, even when they wrap.

examples.title: Handle long words
examples.description: Long links or words can force a box wider than its screen.
examples.output: The long word wraps inside the narrow card instead of pushing the layout sideways.

examples.title: Make tables usable on narrow screens
examples.description: A table may need more width than a phone.
examples.code:
Friday clubs
ClubRoomTime
GardenSchool yardAfter lunch
examples.output: On a narrow screen, only the table region can scroll sideways. Its name explains the region to a reading tool.

examples.title: Respond to a component width
examples.description: A container query checks the size of a chosen parent box.
examples.code:
Moon Trip

A short space story.
examples.output: The card switches to a row when its container, not the viewport, is at least 25rem wide.

examples.title: Test real content and zoom
examples.description: A responsive layout needs testing with real words and larger text.
examples.code:
Check a narrow phone-sized width.
Check a wide desktop width.
Try a very long title.
Zoom the page to 200%.
Use Tab through every control.
Check that reading does not need sideways scrolling.
examples.output: You learn which part needs a flexible size, a wrap rule or more space.
